general_information.Description: This course provides students with practical knowledge and skills to design, deploy, and operate end-to-end MLOps pipelines on cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud). Students will master cloud-native data engineering (S3/GCS, Kafka, Dataflow, Glue), data versioning with DVC, feature stores (Feast, Vertex Feature Store), and scalable model training using distributed GPU/TPU clusters. The curriculum covers CI/CD for ML (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI), containerization with Docker, Kubernetes-based deployment (GKE/EKS/AKS), and production monitoring with Prometheus, Grafana, and cloud-native logging. Through hands-on labs and a final cloud-deployed project, students will gain comprehensive experience in building production-ready ML systems with automated monitoring, drift detection, and retraining pipelines, while addressing cost optimization, security, and compliance (GDPR, HIPAA).
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are responsible for completing all exercises, assignments, 4 labs, and 2 process tests assigned by the instructor in class or at home, and submitting them on time. - Students must complete a final group project (end-to-end MLOps pipeline on cloud) and submit a 4–6 page scientific paper describing the architecture, experiments, ops plan, and cost analysis. - Laptops are to be used in class strictly for learning purposes. - Students must promptly access the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information.
general_information.Tools: Python, AWS (SageMaker, Lambda, ECR, GKE/EKS/AKS), Google Cloud (Vertex AI, Cloud Composer, GCR), Azure (Azure ML, ACR), Docker, Kubernetes, DVC, MLflow, Feast, TFX, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, Evidently AI, FastAPI, TensorFlow Serving.
general_information.Note: - The course adopts a practice oriented, PBL (project base learning) approach in which students progressively design, deploy, monitor, and maintain an end to end cloud native ML (Machine Learning) system throughout the semester. - Students complete four hands on laboratory assignments focusing on cloud data versioning and orchestration, TFX pipelines and model validation, containerization and Kubernetes deployment, and monitoring with automated retraining. Labs are completed individually or in assigned teams and submitted before the specified deadlines. - Two computer based multiple choice Progress Tests evaluate students' theoretical understanding of Cloud MLOps, cloud architecture, data engineering, MLOps pipelines, CI/CD, containerization, deployment, and monitoring concepts. - Two Process Tests assess practical competencies through production-oriented scenarios, including incident response, drift detection, rollback strategies, model promotion, CI/CD execution, and deployment validation. - The mandatory team based capstone project requires students to design and implement a complete cloud native MLOps solution, supported by an end-to-end pipeline, technical documentation, cost analysis, a scientific paper, and an in class presentation with a live demonstration. - The final examination is an individual computer-based multiple choice test covering all major Cloud MLOps concepts and practices. - The final course grade is calculated as follows: Progress Test 1 (10%), Progress Test 2 (10%), Lab 1 (7.5%), Lab 2 (7.5%), Lab 3 (7.5%), Lab 4 (7.5%), Process Test 1 (7.5%), Process Test 2 (7.5%), Final Project (20%), and Final Examination (10%). - Completion Criteria: All assessments must score above 0, with a minimum Final Examination score of 4.0 and an overall course grade of 5.0.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand core concepts, differences, and relationships among MLOps, DevOps, DataOps, and LLMOps (including RAG & Prompt Engineering basics); apply cloud architecture patterns for ML systems (ingestion, storage, deployment models) across major cloud platforms (AWS SageMaker, Azure ML, Vertex AI).

Design and implement cloud-based data engineering pipelines using cloud-native services (AWS Lambda/Step Functions/Glue, GCP Dataflow/Cloud Composer, Azure Data Factory) and implement feature store management solutions (Feast, Vertex/Azure Feature Store) for offline/online inference.

Apply experiment tracking tools (MLflow, WandB, SageMaker Experiments, Vertex Vizier) and data versioning principles using DVC with cloud remotes (S3/GCS/Azure) to ensure reproducibility, data lineage, and metadata management in ML experiments.
Design and build end-to-end TensorFlow Extended (TFX) and cloud native pipelines (including ExampleGen, Transform, Trainer, Evaluator, Publisher), establish model baselines, and handle concept drift.
Understand feature store concepts and implement feature management solutions using Feast, Vertex Feature Store, or Azure Feature Stores for offline/online inference on cloud.

Apply Docker containerization best practices, build containerized MLOps pipelines to deploy to cloud registries (ECR/GCR/ACR) and services (Cloud Run, ECS, GKE, AKS), and implement model serving patterns (TF Serving, FastAPI, Flask) with progressive delivery (blue-green, canary) and autoscaling (HPA/VPA).

Implement automated CI/CD pipelines for ML using GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or GitLab CI integrated with cloud services to automate model deployments, testing, and continuous validation in cloud environments.

Implement continuous model monitoring (Prometheus, Grafana, Cloud Monitoring) for data/concept drift, setup automated retraining triggers based on performance thresholds, and apply operational excellence principles (incident response, runbooks, rollback, data governance, GDPR, HIPAA, IAM).

Implement an end-to-end Cloud MLOps capstone project encompassing infrastructure setup, automated data pipelines, model tracking, cloud deployment, monitoring, automated retraining, and document it via a scientific/technical paper (4–6 pages) detailing architecture, experiments, ops plan, and cost analysis.

assessments.Category: Final Project: End-to-End Cloud MLOps Pipeline + Scientific Paper
assessments.Question Type: Group Project + Scientific Paper (4–6 pages) + Live Demo + Git Repository
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Design and implement a complete cloud-native MLOps pipeline including data ingestion, versioning, training, validation, deployment, monitoring, automated retraining, cost analysis, architecture documentation and reproducibility
assessments.Grading Guide: Submitted via LMS, Git repository and live demonstration; evaluated by instructor using project rubric
assessments.Note: Grading distribution: Demo (40%), Scientific Paper (30%), Repository & Reproducibility (20%), Peer Evaluation (10%).

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Configure DVC with cloud storage (S3/GCS/Azure Blob), build ETL pipeline using Airflow/Cloud Composer, implement data lineage and reproducibility
assessments.Grading Guide: Submitted via LMS and Git repository; instructor executes pipeline and evaluates reproducibility
assessments.Note: Repository must execute successfully; documentation and reproducibility are mandatory.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Build complete TFX pipeline (ExampleGen, Transform, Trainer, Evaluator), perform TFMA evaluation and model validation
assessments.Grading Guide: Instructor validates pipeline execution, evaluation reports and testing results
assessments.Note: Pipeline must execute without critical errors; evaluation report required.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Docker image creation, cloud container registry (ECR/GCR/ACR), Kubernetes Deployment & Service, health monitoring
assessments.Grading Guide: Submitted through Git repository with deployed endpoint demonstration
assessments.Note: Dockerfile quality, deployment reproducibility and endpoint availability are evaluated.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Implement Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, alert rules, automated retraining workflow using cloud events
assessments.Grading Guide: Instructor verifies monitoring dashboard, alert notifications and retraining execution
assessments.Note: Students must demonstrate complete monitoring and automated response workflow.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Diagnose production drift, identify root cause, rollback deployment, update monitoring and incident documentation
assessments.Grading Guide: Conducted in laboratory under instructor supervision
assessments.Note: Assessment rubric includes recovery time, correctness of rollback procedure, documentation quality and teamwork.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Execute CI/CD workflow from validated model to canary deployment and full production rollout with reproducibility verification
assessments.Grading Guide: Conducted in laboratory under instructor supervision
assessments.Note: Rubric evaluates CI/CD correctness, deployment strategy, testing coverage and documentation.
